subject: physics
title: Nuclear fusion
key_idea: (Separate science) In **nuclear fusion** two light nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus. Some of the mass is converted into energy of radiation. Fusion powers the Sun and other stars, but it needs a very high temperature and pressure.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Fusion is the joining of two light nuclei. This section covers what happens and why it releases energy.

items.meaning: The joining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus.
The centre of an atom. Fusion joins nuclei, not whole atoms.

items: Two **hydrogen** nuclei (isotopes of hydrogen) join to make a **helium** nucleus.
The total mass of the particles decreases.
Some of the mass is converted into **energy of radiation**.
Fusion is the energy source for stars, including the Sun.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Fusion does not happen at low temperatures and pressures. The reason is the force between the nuclei.

items: All nuclei are positively charged, because they contain **protons**.
Two nuclei repel each other because they have the same charge.
A very **high temperature** gives the nuclei enough energy to overcome the repulsion.
A high pressure and density bring the nuclei close enough together.

blocks.text: The difficulty of making fusion power

items: It is hard to maintain the high temperature and the high pressure.
The hot fusion gases are hard to contain.
These conditions are difficult to produce on Earth, so a practical and economic power station does not exist yet.

blocks.text: Benefits, and a claim that was not believed

items: Fusion has benefits: it would give more energy for the same mass of fuel, the fuel is easy to obtain, and the waste has a short half-life.
In 1989 a claim of fusion at room temperature was not believed. The results were not peer reviewed and no other scientist could repeat them.

checks.q: Explain how nuclear fusion releases energy.
checks.a: Light nuclei fuse to form a heavier nucleus. Some of the mass is converted into energy of radiation.

checks.q: Explain why a very high temperature is needed for two hydrogen nuclei to fuse.
checks.a: A high temperature means the nuclei have high energy. This is needed to overcome the repulsion between the nuclei, because they have the same charge.

checks.q: Describe one difference between fission and fusion.
checks.a: Any one from: in fusion nuclei join and in fission nuclei split; fusion needs a higher temperature and pressure; a larger nucleus forms in fusion and smaller nuclei in fission; fission causes a chain reaction but fusion does not.

answer_points: To form heavier nuclei or elements.
Some of the mass of the nuclei is converted into energy of radiation.

answer_points: A high temperature means high energy.
This is needed to overcome the force of repulsion.

worked_example.question: Scientists think that nuclear fusion would be a better energy source than nuclear fission. A fission power station uses uranium, has a power output of 1.0 × 10⁹ W and its waste is very radioactive with a long half-life. A fusion power station uses hydrogen, is expected to have a power output of 1.3 × 10⁹ W and its waste is slightly radioactive with a short half-life. Use the information to compare a nuclear fission power station with a nuclear fusion power station. In your answer, write about the differences between a fission reaction and a fusion reaction, the benefits of using nuclear fusion instead of fission, and the difficulties associated with using nuclear fusion.
answer_points: Fission is the splitting of a large (uranium) nucleus into lighter nuclei and neutrons, and a chain reaction occurs which has to be controlled.
Fusion is the combining of lighter (hydrogen) nuclei into a heavier (helium) nucleus.
Benefits: the fusion power station is expected to output 1.3 times more power, so fewer are needed.
Fission waste is more radioactive and has a longer half-life, so it stays dangerous for longer and has to be stored.
Uranium is non-renewable, but hydrogen is renewable and more easily obtained.
Difficulty: fusion needs a high temperature and pressure, which is difficult to produce on Earth.
worked_example.tip: Level-marked. Cover the difference between the reactions, the benefits and the difficulties, using the data.

worked_example.question:
Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen (H) with 1 proton and 1 neutron. Nuclear fusion occurs when two nuclei of deuterium combine. An isotope of helium (He) and a neutron are formed.

Use nuclide notation to write down the nuclide equation for this reaction.
answer_points: ²₁H + ²₁H on the left-hand side.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Fusion can be written as a nuclide equation. The mass numbers balance and the proton numbers balance.

items: (Supplement) The total mass of the nucleus formed is slightly smaller than the total mass of the nuclei that joined.
(Supplement) The mass difference is released as energy.
In a stable star, such as the Sun, hydrogen fuses into helium in the core.
Research is being carried out to find how the energy from fusion can be used to produce electricity on a large scale.

worked_example.question:
This question is about nuclear fusion.

Explain why a fusion reaction will only happen at high temperature and high pressure.
answer_points: At low temperature the nuclei move too slowly, and collide less often.
The nuclei cannot get close enough together to fuse.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score the 3 marks. High temperature and pressure give the opposite of each point.
